speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing hand tremors and recent memory issues; to help me understand the severity of your condition, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the tremor has been worsening over a year and is now affecting fine motor skills like reading, could you describe whether the shaking is more prominent when he is holding his hands out or when he is at rest? Additionally, has he noticed any stiffness in his arms or legs, or a feeling that his limbs move more slowly than usual?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease. The combination of a unilateral resting tremor, bradykinesia (implied by stiffness/slow movement), masked facies (reduced facial expressions), and cognitive decline is highly suggestive of this neurodegenerative disorder. I will proceed to order a DaTscan and MRI to rule out atypical parkinsonism.
